messages.author: ff7308de7d8c1c01
messages.subject: Bilat.symmetry function, version upgrade issue?
parts:
Hello,

I was interested in using the compare.CR function, so I decided to take the plunge and upgrade from geomorph 3.0.7 to version 3.1.3.

However, I now run into a problem when re-running the code for bilat.symmetry: 

primates_sym <- bilat.symmetry(primates$coords, ind=dimnames(primates$coords)[[3]], side = NULL, replicate=NULL, object.sym=T, land.pairs=pairedLM).

it now gives me the following error:
"Error in matrix(PSh$ANOVA$df[nrow(RSS) + 1], nrow(RSS), ncol(RSS)) : 
  non-numeric matrix extent" 

Yet, as far as I can see, this is the same data input as before me upgrading (no issues under 3.0.7) and cannot figure out what may be causing the non-numeric matrix extent. I checked to see if perhaps changes were made to this function, but this does not appear to be the case. In order to make sure I didn't do something stupid, I also checked using a published piece of code (not mine) and it now returns to same error (before the upgrade it did not). 

Has anybody else encountered this issue, and if so how did you resolve it?

Best wishes,
Katrien

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Bilat.symmetry function, version upgrade issue?
parts:
Just a quick note to everyone in the geomorphoverse…

Katrien’s issue was solved by updating RRPP, the main package on which geomorph depends, and which does the “under the hood” workhorse stuff that makes many of the geomorph functions possible.  When installing or updating geomorph, it is a good practice to not trust CRAN (and cannot trust Github in this way at all) that RRPP will also be updated.  Rather, I recommend that when you install or update geomorph, you do the same with RRPP, just to be safe.  

We usually submit updates to CRAN for both packages at the same time, so it is possible to get out of sync updating just one.

Happy computing!
Mike
